title: What a One-Hour Interview Does Not Tell an LLM About You: Interviews Elicit Traits, Not Decision Policies
abstract: arXiv:2605.29458v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly asked to stand in for particular people, and interviewing the person is the natural way to tell a model who they are. We test what a one-hour LLM-led adaptive interview tells a model about an individual's value-laden decisions. 46 adults completed such an interview and then answered 25 dilemma questions, which are the ground truth. We predict their answers from different parts of the transcript, compare adaptive follow-up questions with fixed ones on the same participants, and benchmark every variant against a model given no information about the person and against the majority answer. No part of the interview is reliably better than either baseline, and adaptive follow-ups are no better than fixed ones. Two audits of the transcripts show why. translated_title: 一小时访谈无法告诉大语言模型关于你的什么：访谈捕捉的是人格特质，而非决策策略
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型越来越多地被要求代表特定的人，而访谈这个人本身是让模型了解其身份的自然方式。我们测试了由LLM主导的一小时自适应访谈能让模型了解到个人在价值相关决策上的多少信息。46名成年人完成了这样的访谈，随后回答了25个两难问题，这些答案作为真实基准。我们从转录文本的不同部分预测他们的答案，在同一批参与者上比较自适应追问与固定问题，并将每种变体与无任何个人信息的模型以及多数答案基线进行比较。结果显示，访谈的任何部分都没有可靠地优于任何基线，自适应追问也不比固定问题更好。对转录文本的两项审计揭示了原因：在85%的预测错误中，审计员找不到任何能将该个体的选择与其他选项区分开来的证据，而在转录文本确实包含相关信息时……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 一小时LLM访谈无法可靠预测个人在价值两难问题上的真实决策——访谈捕捉到的是人格特质而非具体的决策策略，且大多数预测错误源于转录文本中根本缺乏区分个体选择的关键证据。
en_tdlr: A one-hour LLM-led interview fails to reliably predict individuals' value-laden decisions—interviews elicit personality traits rather than decision policies, and most prediction errors stem from transcripts lacking evidence that distinguishes a person's choices from alternatives.
